issue.title: ceos_topo_converger: LACP channel-group not updated for converged peers on LAG topologies

failure.body:
## Description

When using `use_converged_peers: true` on LAG topologies (e.g., t1-lag), the `ceos_topo_converger.py` does not update the `lacp` (channel-group) field when remapping Ethernet interfaces for converged peers. All interfaces end up in `channel-group 1` instead of being distributed across Port-Channels.

## Root Cause

In `ceos_topo_converger.py` around line 165, when building VRF interface configs:

```python
vrf[eth_intf] = deepcopy(peer_intfs[intf])
```

The `lacp` field is copied as-is from the original peer config. Each original peer has `Ethernet1: lacp=1, Ethernet2: lacp=1` (channel-group 1 → Po1). After convergence, all 16 Ethernet interfaces (from 8 spines) retain `lacp=1`, so all end up in `channel-group 1` on the cEOS container.

## Observed Behavior

On the spine cEOS container after `add-topo`:
- `show running-config | section channel-group`: all 16 Ethernet interfaces have `channel-group 1`
- Port-Channel1 has 16 members (only 2 can actually bundle via LACP)
- Port-Channel2 through Port-Channel8 have zero members
- On the DUT, only 1 of 8 PortChannels comes up (whichever happens to match)

## Expected Behavior

- Et1,Et2 → channel-group 1 (Po1)
- Et3,Et4 → channel-group 2 (Po2)
- ...
- Et15,Et16 → channel-group 8 (Po8)

All 8 PortChannels should come up with 2 members each.

## Fix

Add LACP channel-group update after the `deepcopy`:

```python
vrf[eth_intf] = deepcopy(peer_intfs[intf])
# Update lacp channel-group to match the new Port-Channel index
if "lacp" in vrf[eth_intf] and "Port-Channel1" in peer_intfs:
    vrf[eth_intf]["lacp"] = intf_index
```

This has been validated locally — all 8 PortChannels come up with correct 2-member distribution, and all 24 BGP sessions establish.

## Environment

- Topology: t1-lag with `use_converged_peers: true`
- cEOS: `ceosimage:4.32.5M`
- Testbed: KVM virtual switch

## Related

- #22524 (converged peers: topo_is_multi_vrf not set for tests)

resolution.title: Fix LACP channel-group assignment in ceos_topo_converger for converged peers
resolution.description:
## Description

Fix a bug in `ceos_topo_converger.py` where the LACP channel-group number is not updated when remapping Ethernet interfaces for converged peers on LAG topologies.

### What is the motivation for this PR?

When using `use_converged_peers: true` on LAG topologies (e.g., t1-lag), the converger copies interface configs via `deepcopy` but retains the original `lacp` value (always `1`). This causes all Ethernet interfaces in the converged cEOS container to join `channel-group 1` instead of being distributed across separate Port-Channels.

**Before fix (t1-lag, 8 spines converged into 1 cEOS):**
- All 16 Ethernet interfaces → `channel-group 1` (Po1)
- Po1 has 16 members (only 2 can LACP bundle), Po2-Po8 have zero members
- Only 1 of 8 PortChannels comes up on the DUT

**After fix:**
- Et1,Et2 → channel-group 1; Et3,Et4 → channel-group 2; ... Et15,Et16 → channel-group 8
- All 8 PortChannels come up with correct 2-member distribution
- All 24 BGP sessions establish

### How did you do it?

After the `deepcopy` of the peer interface config, update the `lacp` field to match the new Port-Channel index (`intf_index`):

```python
vrf[eth_intf] = deepcopy(peer_intfs[intf])
if "lacp" in vrf[eth_intf] and "Port-Channel1" in peer_intfs:
    vrf[eth_intf]["lacp"] = intf_index
```

### How did you verify/test it?

Validated on a KVM testbed with t1-lag topology and `use_converged_peers: true`:
- Verified `show running-config | section channel-group` on spine cEOS shows correct distribution
- All 8 PortChannels up with 2 members each on DUT
- All 24/24 BGP sessions established (8 T2 spines + 16 T0 ToRs)

Fixes #22525
